flawed_step: Lines 0034–0037 incorrectly conclude that the desired condition is violated merely because the upper bound (n+1)/2 exceeds n/2. An upper bound exceeding the target does not show that the actual component size exceeds it.
counterexample: Let T be the path u-w-v-y on n=4 vertices. Remove the leaf u, obtaining T'=w-v-y. Choose v as the inductive vertex; T'-v has components {w} and {y}, each of size 1 <= (n-1)/2=3/2, and v != w. Restoring u attaches it to {w}, producing the component {u,w} of size 2=n/2; the other component {y} has size 1. Thus v still satisfies the desired condition, despite (n+1)/2=5/2 being greater than n/2=2.
assessment_summary: The proof first fails at lines 0034–0037 by treating a loose upper bound as an attained component size. The explicit four-vertex path shows that Case 2 need not violate the condition.
